Name: Seasonal Goth Sebastian
Author: alphania
Description:
[size=4]
[b]This mod is meant to work alongside Poltergeisters[/b] [/size][url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5450?tab=description][size=4]Seasonal Outfits - Slightly Cuter Aesthetic[/size]
[/url]
[color=#ffe599][size=3][b]It won't work unless you have that mod installed.[/b][/size][/color]

This is my first ever mod, and it was a much larger project than I initially predicted. At first I just wanted a new hairstyle for Sebby, so I drew a crappy one (since it was my first experience with pixel art), used it for a day and wasn't contended with how it looked. It then evolved into this mod, because I just can't seem to settle with easy.

I couldn't have finished this project in the first place without all the amazing support I've received from the mod community in the Stardew Valley discord channel. Thank you all for making this possible!

Since I'm a total newbie with modding I've tweaked this code template created by AirynS [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/14983?tab=description]Seasonal outfits code template
[/url]

[size=4][b]Mod content[/b][/size]:

This mod replaces all portraits and sprites in the Seasonal Outfits mod with Sebastian's new Goth appearance.

There's an option whether to use a headpiece in Sebastian's Spirit's Eve costume. It's attached by default, but if you want to remove it just run the game once in order to create a [b]config.json[/b] file in the mod folder, open it and switch from [b]true[/b] to [b]false[/b] in order to remove the headpiece.
Or you can use [url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/5098]Generic Mod Config Menu
[/url]
[color=#93c47d]
[b][size=3]Caution:[/size][/b][/color][size=2]Because of how the hair is shaded and the dark clothes, these portraits will not look good on a very dark or black background[/size].


[b][size=4]Installation:[/size][/b]

[list]
[*]Download and extract the file into your mod folder
[/list]

To [b]uninstall[/b], just remove this file from your mod folder.
